findings: The 2026-11-07 canonical parent gives purpose and two same-use-case variant routes for Checkout Sessions API with embedded components and Payment Intents API with Elements (new raw lines 5–14; old raw lines 8–16 and 558–566). Both were detailed in the April 21, 2026 capture. The parent index supplies navigation and does not refresh integration requirements.

The April Checkout Sessions variant says Elements saved methods support cards and ACH Direct Debit. The merchant enables the saving checkbox at Session creation, supplying an existing v1 Customer or customer-configured v2 Account, or the shown customer_creation=always path. Authenticate the returning customer before supplying the corresponding ID. The then-latest Stripe.js defaults enableSave/enableRedisplay to auto in the described enabled configuration. For custom UI, disable built-ins, separately collect consent, pass savePaymentMethod or the selected paymentMethod ID at confirmation, and render only entries returned in savedPaymentMethods, which the guide limits to allow_redisplay=always (old raw lines 18–82, 130–176, 230–291, 331–347, 402–406 and 482–484).

The Payment Intents Payment Element feature uses matching customer identity on the PaymentIntent and CustomerSession and both respective client secrets for the saved-method UI, with the documented CustomerSession-secret omission after a creation error. Stripe.js applies setup_future_usage and allow_redisplay based on the save checkbox at confirmation. Intent autoflagging and CustomerSession payment_method_save_usage cannot both be explicitly set for the same transaction. A PaymentIntent override can save without that checkout checkbox, while the same guide directs disabling the override on the server if the customer declines and retaining purpose-specific consent (old raw lines 572–583, 605–618, 628–695, 697–729 and 747–753).

The dated Payment Intents material uses payment_method_options.card.setup_future_usage to illustrate saving only supported methods. For later payments use the correct customer or customer_account and PaymentMethod ID, create and confirm a separate off-session Intent, and handle the possible authentication error if an exemption is unavailable. The April guide describes generation of a reusable sepa_debit PaymentMethod when Bancontact/iDEAL/Sofort are set up for future use, with delayed processing before success or requires_payment_method in the documented SEPA path. Test email/token outcomes remain test fixtures (old raw lines 747–753, 804–853 and 897–956).

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-save-during-payment-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-save-during-payment-elements-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-save-during-payment-elements.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/save-during-payment`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: https://docs.stripe.com/payments/save-during-payment gives a two-variant selector at new raw lines 5–14. The April 21, 2026 implementation in old raw lines 18–82, 130–176, 331–347, 402–406, 605–618, 697–729 and 804–853 distinguishes Checkout Sessions with Elements, which enables the save-consent UI for cards and ACH Direct Debit, from a PaymentIntent with a server-created CustomerSession for saved-method features. The merchant provides the correct Customer or customer-configured Account identity and, for redisplay and later use, records the customer's purpose-specific consent. Stripe.js applies the checkbox response to the saving and redisplay settings in the Payment Intents route. Eligible prior methods can be used for a later, separate PaymentIntent. Off-session authentication can fail, and SEPA Debit can stay processing before a final result. source-stripe-save-during-payment-elements.md needs the Elements-specific restriction, eligible redisplay, consent and optional CustomerSession-secret fallback qualified.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/save-during-payment, new raw lines 9–14 present the same two web route labels found at old raw lines 8–16 and 558–566. This is navigation and presentation rather than evidence of a substantive workflow change or withdrawal. Keep the April 21, 2026 implementation and November 7, 2026 index as separately dated evidence in source-stripe-save-during-payment-elements.md, with the reciprocal stripe-saved-payment-methods route. Preserve the distinction between Checkout Sessions with Elements and PaymentIntents and the Accounts v2 preview/version boundary. Preserve authorized redisplay, the card/ACH scope, the server-side disable instruction when a buyer declines, and the documented fallback when CustomerSession creation fails (old raw lines 18–52, 402–406, 605–618, 697–729 and 747–753). The setup override bypasses the UI checkbox’s save behavior, while the merchant still has the guide’s explicit consent and recordkeeping responsibilities. The April PaymentIntent examples enable payment_method_remove (old raw lines 636–649 and 676–689). The separate April 21 Payment Element reference (raw/stripe-payment-element-saved-payment-methods-2025.md lines 48–50) says removal through Saved also removes the method from an ongoing subscription using it. Keep that dated warning with the example or link directly to it. Stripe recommends disabling Payment Element removal and routing changes through account settings where subscriptions are visible.
